item.intervention: Replaced one of the two classical EAM potentials in the TOR-TILD method with a Machine Learning Potential (MTP) and replaced thermodynamic integration (TI) with free energy perturbation (FEP).
item.processing: Used a hierarchically structured approach: EAM for coexistence, MTP for liquid reference, and FEP for DFT correction. Calculated on a 5x6 (V,T) grid.
item.test_conditions: Computational efficiency comparison on a 5x6 (V,T) grid using LDA exchange-correlation functional.
item.structure_change: Not stated
item.property_change: Computational resources saved by about 80% compared to the hybrid TOR-TILD method; total CPU time reduced from 1,384,739 core hours (Hybrid) to 285,802 core hours (New).
item.attributed_mechanism: The MTP provides a strong overlap with the ab initio liquid phase space, enabling efficient free energy perturbation calculations and avoiding expensive ab initio MD thermodynamic integration.
quotes: The method achieves overall savings of computational resources by 80% compared to current alternatives.
When comparing the new approach with the hybrid TOR-TILD method, the required computational resources are saved by about 80% in calculating a free energy surface on a 5 × 6 ( V , T ) grid.
The overall acceleration is attributed to substituting EAM with MTP and TI with FEP.

item.intervention: Included electronic excitations and their coupling to vibrations in the free energy calculation using finite temperature DFT.
item.processing: Calculated the electronic density of states (DOS) at 2400 K for solid and liquid phases using GGA-PBE and LDA functionals.
item.test_conditions: Temperature T = 2400 K at respective equilibrium volumes.
item.structure_change: Thermal vibrations smooth out the DOS of both the solid and liquid phase at elevated temperatures.
item.property_change: Electronic Gibbs energy difference of 4.2 meV/atom between solid and liquid (GGA-PBE), leading to a melting point shift of 48 K compared to calculations without electronic contribution.
item.attributed_mechanism: The disparity in electronic contribution results from a gap of 0.16 states/eV ⋅ atom in the DOS of solid and liquid phases at the Fermi level.
quotes: This disparity results from a gap of 0.16 states/eV ⋅ atom in the DOS of solid and liquid phases at the Fermi level.

Correspondingly, this gap translates to an electronic Gibbs energy difference of 4.2 meV/atom between the solid and liquid, leading to a shift in the melting point by 48 K compared to calculations that do not account for the electronic contribution.
For the LDA calculations, the electronic Gibbs energy difference between solid and liquid is about 5.8 meV/atom resulting in a melting point shift by 57 K.

item.intervention: Included short-range order (SRO) contributions to the solid Gibbs energy using on-lattice machine learning potentials.
item.processing: Performed Monte Carlo simulations at 2260 K to compute configurational internal energy, entropy, and free energy referenced to the ideal random alloy.
item.test_conditions: Temperature 2260 K (approx. 100 K below GGA-PBE melting point) to fix volume and electronic free energy contributions.
item.structure_change: Configurational entropy is slightly smaller than the ideal configurational entropy of ln(4).
item.property_change: SRO stabilizes the solid phase by about 2.4 meV/atom, resulting in a slight shift of the melting temperature (approx. 25 K).
item.attributed_mechanism: SRO decreases the internal energy by about 8–9 meV/atom, which outweighs the positive (destabilizing) entropy-driven energy contribution of around 5–6 meV/atom.
quotes: However, SRO also decreases the internal energy by about 8–9 meV/atom (Fig. 4 d).
Hence the resulting free energy of the solid is overall stabilized by about 2.4 meV/atom, Fig. 4 a, resulting in a slight shift of the melting temperature as discussed further below.

item.intervention: Changed the exchange-correlation functional from GGA-PBE to LDA.
item.processing: Computed melting properties using both GGA-PBE and LDA functionals within the proposed free energy perturbation framework.
item.test_conditions: Melting property calculation for TaVCrW.
item.structure_change: Not stated
item.property_change: Melting point increased from 2376 K (GGA-PBE) to 2409 K (LDA); Enthalpy of fusion decreased from 268.5 meV/atom (GGA-PBE) to 265.5 meV/atom (LDA).
item.attributed_mechanism: The difference is attributed to the underbinding/overbinding property of GGA-PBE/LDA, though the text notes this rule may not hold for TaVCrW due to discrepancies in unary lattice constants.
quotes: Our DFT predicted melting points from GGA-PBE and LDA are respectively 2376 K and 2409 K.

Our predicted enthalpy of fusion, the entropy of fusion, the heat capacity of both solid and liquid, and the volume change at the corresponding melting point are slightly larger than the calphad values, whereas the predicted volumes for solid and liquid are smaller than the calphad values.
The reason is attributed to the underbinding / overbinding property of GGA-PBE / LDA.

item.intervention: Compared the new method's results against CALPHAD extrapolated values.
item.processing: Extrapolated melting properties using the CALPHAD method with Thermo-Calc 2023a and the TCHEA4 database.
item.test_conditions: Comparison of DFT predicted melting properties with CALPHAD data.
item.structure_change: Not stated
item.property_change: DFT predicted melting points (2376 K GGA-PBE, 2409 K LDA) are lower than the CALPHAD value (2569 K) by 193 K and 160 K respectively.
item.attributed_mechanism: The discrepancy is attributed to uncertainties in the CALPHAD extrapolation (based on binary subsystems) and potential DFT errors (statistics, fitting, magnetic fluctuations), rather than the methodology itself.

First, for the CALPHAD extracted melting point, the input data in the high entropy alloy database for parametrization includes only sub-binary alloy information for TaVCrW.

item.intervention: Replaced the expensive thermodynamic integration (TI) step with free energy perturbation (FEP) for the MTP to DFT correction.
item.processing: Used approximately 28 uncorrelated snapshots from MTP trajectories to compute the energy difference between MTP and DFT.
item.test_conditions: Liquid TaVCrW at T = 2400 K and V = 16.24 Å³/atom.
item.structure_change: Not stated
item.property_change: The energy difference between FEP and TI approaches is only 0.5 meV/atom, resulting in a melting point shift of 15 K.
item.attributed_mechanism: The MTP provides a strong overlap with the phase space distribution of the ab initio liquid, enabling efficient FEP calculations.
quotes: The resulting energy difference between the free energy perturbation and the thermodynamic integration approach is only 0.5 meV/atom.
These energy differences result in a comparably small melting point shift of 15 K.
This overlap enables more efficient free energy perturbation calculations and avoids the computationally expensive thermodynamic integration calculations based on ab initio MD.

item.structure_change: Not stated

item.intervention: Used a specially designed Machine Learning Potential (MTP) optimized for the liquid phase.
item.processing: MTP optimized for accurate description of the DFT phase space representative of the liquid; used in conjunction with EAM for coexistence.
item.test_conditions: Liquid free energy calculations for multi-component alloys.
item.structure_change: Not stated
item.property_change: The MTP has an RMSE of 2.6 meV/atom for GGA-PBE calculations.
item.attributed_mechanism: The MTP functions only as a very efficient bridge to obtain DFT-accurate thermodynamics of the liquid phase; it is not guaranteed to be transferable to other parts of the DFT phase space.
quotes: A key ingredient to the proposed methodology is an optimized machine-learning potential (here, an MTP) that replaces one of the two classical EAM potentials utilized within the TOR-TILD method.
It is important to stress that the MTP involved in the proposed method is solely optimized for an accurate description of the part of the DFT phase space representative of the liquid.
According to the RMSE of the MTP (here 2.6 meV/atom for GGA-PBE calculations), to attain an accuracy of 1 meV/atom, only approximately 28 uncorrelated snapshots are needed.
